# R-RBS-LM Finding 584 (STANDING RULE — the kernel-persistence model: the Class-L eigenbasis is the disk SSoT; the the_one-ladder loop-bookshelf of tomes is LATENT in it and regenerated by cheap HDC at inference; you do NOT lossy-flatten the shelf into one hypervector) — **Pinned as the standing rule for EVERY kernel (including Egyptian), at the user's direction. THE RULE: the KERNEL = the Class-L co-occurrence eigenbasis V + vocab is the on-disk single-source-of-truth — compact and lossless. The the_one-ladder LOOP-BOOKSHELF of tomes (the inference-time memory structure) is LATENT in the kernel and REGENERATED by cheap HDC at inference (tome routing = a free `atan2` read-out of two V columns, F542; tome volumes = cheap Class-M bundles). The shelf was NEVER the stored thing. You do NOT lossy-flatten the bookshelf into a single hypervector for disk — that re-introduces the exact superposition capacity-collapse the tome-shelf was invented to fix (F529/F532/F533). DEMONSTRATED by contrast on a real Class-L kernel (TLA Demotic, 200 lemmas, 8,456 edges): (A) KERNEL-PERSIST (correct) — persist V + vocab; the loop-shelf regenerates deterministically + losslessly by cheap atan2 routing (words spread 12/14 tomes; per-word identity exact because each word is its own V row); the shelf is reconstructed for free. (B) SINGLE-HV FLATTEN (the anti-pattern) — bundle N word-HVs into ONE hypervector; membership recall COLLAPSES with N (100% @ 7 → 100% @ 31 → 92% @ 127 → 79% @ 199), i.e. a single flattened HV cannot hold the shelf — exactly the capacity failure the tome-shelf fixes. So: persist the kernel (lossless, compact, shelf-latent); never collapse the shelf to one HV; a kernel is a LOOP bookshelf of tomes (F544: loop, not flat circle — conjugation mirror, parity-free, multi-directional), not a single hypervector object. This is the anchor that keeps us from accidentally building a single-HV kernel again — for Egyptian (F582: the Class-M category anchors are the seed/volume; the loop-shelf precipitates when the Layer-2 Class-L corpus kernel is built) and for every kernel.**

## Result (demonstration on a real Class-L kernel, TLA Demotic, 200 lemmas)
| model | persist | inference recall |
|---|---|---|
| **(A) KERNEL-PERSIST (correct)** | V + vocab (compact, lossless) | loop-shelf regenerated by cheap `atan2` routing; **deterministic + lossless**; per-word identity exact |
| **(B) SINGLE-HV FLATTEN (anti-pattern)** | one bundled HV | membership recall **100% (7) → 92% (127) → 79% (199)** — collapses with N |

## Verdict (the standing rule)
**The kernel is the disk SSoT; the loop-shelf is latent.** Persist the Class-L eigenbasis V + vocab — compact and lossless. The the_one-ladder loop-bookshelf of tomes is **latent** in it and regenerated by **cheap HDC at inference** (tome routing = a free `atan2` read-out of V, F542; tome volumes = cheap Class-M bundles). The shelf was never the stored thing.

**Do not lossy-flatten the shelf into one HV.** Membership recall collapses with N (panel B) — the exact superposition capacity failure the tome-shelf exists to fix (F529/F532/F533). A kernel is a **loop bookshelf of tomes** (F544: loop, not flat circle — conjugation mirror, parity-free, multi-directional), **not a single hypervector**.

**Applies to every kernel, including Egyptian** (F582): the Class-M category anchors are the seed/volume; the loop-shelf precipitates when the Layer-2 Class-L corpus kernel is built. This is the anchor against accidentally building a single-HV kernel again. Favored not privileged (F398); held open (F394).
